notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l001: The directional phrase Кутпа жагы is clear; the river name looks like Кор but may be a different short proper name. Completion-first direct manuscript transcription; uncertain forms and provisional English are queued for later review.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l003: The first two word shapes read Урушу койчубу, but the inflection and intended syntax are not fully secure.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l004: The opening was overwritten by the scribe; Эч is supplied from the surviving letter traces and phrase context.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l008: The first word resembles Торудай and the final word resembles жыгылган; both are compressed and the simile is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l009: Күндө is the likeliest reading of the opening word, though its second syllable is lightly written.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l010: The manuscript appears to separate Күн ырысы; the semantic rendering is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l011: The first word visibly resembles Жолон but may represent an uncommon or nonstandard form; English follows the apparent sense.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l012: As in the preceding line, Жолон is a letter-shape reading of an uncertain first word.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l013: Кенен may be the hero's name or an adjective meaning broad; the English preserves it as a proper name.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l014: Боорунан is the closest reading of the opening word; the phrase could carry a more idiomatic sense.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l015: The line is legible, but its repeated киши construction is semantically unusual; translation is literal.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l016: Айда is a best-effort reading of the first word; аркасы тоо киши is clearer and is rendered literally.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l017: The middle word looks like тоңоз but is not securely identifiable; English gives only the probable contextual sense.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l018: Каптан is the visible reading but may be a different ablative noun; translation is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l020: The final form looks like күчүүсү; the resulting hyperbolic comparison is translated literally.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l022: Both Жойгут and the proper name Сурамбек are plausible readings of lightly written names, but neither is fully secure.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l025: The final word reads approximately тооздон and may be a place name or a different common noun.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l026: The first noun is compressed but most likely Берендиги, derived from берен.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l030: The first two words appear to read Кере кабарында, but the phrase is lexically unresolved; English is deliberately literal and provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l031: Тоого is the closest visible reading of the first word, though the construction минип with it is unusual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf011:l032: The opening looks like Үйдө; the phrase is translated literally because its narrative relation is unclear.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l001: The proper name Күнчүк and final verb are plausible readings of compressed cursive; translation is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l003: The proper name and үйдө are the likeliest readings, but both are cursively compressed.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l004: Көрдү is a letter-shape reading and may be another object; English follows it provisionally.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l006: The first and third words appear to be Алга and дүйнө, but the phrase is semantically uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l007: Ойлок may be a proper name; the middle word is especially difficult and the idiomatic English is conjectural.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l009: The last word looks like айтабы; its connection to the preceding noun phrase is uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l010: The first noun is a difficult cursive reading; English gives only the apparent action.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l011: Бейпай and бүркүргөн are plausible letter-shape readings; translation is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l013: The third word appears to be жени but may represent a different lexeme; English takes it as strength.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l016: The final phrase is clearly shaped but its exact idiomatic force is uncertain; English renders the apparent sense.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l019: укумунан is a literal letter-shape reading and may stand for a related word meaning power or force.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l020: Both long words are difficult; the reading and English are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l021: The middle and final words are compressed and overwritten; this is a best-effort contextual reading.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l022: байкасаң is the likeliest reading of faint cursive; the rest is comparatively clear.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l023: кез болуп is a tentative segmentation of the cursive phrase; English follows the broader context.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l024: The phrase кез болгон is tentative, though the sense of the line is reasonably clear.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l025: The last two words are difficult cursive; English conveys the apparent defeat formula.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l026: Боо бербешин is a tentative reading of an idiomatic phrase; translation is contextual.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l029: The final phrase is overwritten and may contain a different noun or adjective; English is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l030: The middle of the line has a struck-out correction; жаның белен is the clearest surviving reading.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf012:l032: бараң appears to be the archaic word for a firearm, but the referent and syntax remain uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf013:l001: The baseline is clear overall, but байкуш and the final case ending are difficult cursive readings.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf013:l002: кысмак is a contextual reading of tightly joined letters; the English is provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf013:l003: The first word appears to be Байдан, but its internal consonant and the phrase's sense are not secure.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf013:l005: The proper name Барак and possessive ending are plausible but compressed in the manuscript.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf013:l006: The two proper names are legible with help from the parallel printed witness; the opening word is faint.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf013:l009: эрендин is the likeliest reading of the middle word, whose initial letters are lightly written.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf013:l010: догонун is a letter-shape reading of an unclear lexeme; translation follows the hostile context.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf013:l011: катташам is plausible from context and letter forms, but its medial cluster is difficult.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf013:l012: The words казат and албууттар fit the visible strokes and context, but both are heavily joined.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf013:l013: чымбары is an unresolved manuscript lexeme; transcription and contextual English are provisional.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf013:l014: The final verb may instead be a closely related form such as тынган; the visible strokes favor тыйылган.
